faq.title: Questions and house rules
faq.text: Everything guests usually ask us before they arrive. If your question is not here, write to us on WhatsApp.
faq.note: These answers describe how we work and are not legal terms. The full booking terms are shown before payment.

questions.q: Is the price the same as on Booking.com?
questions.a: Yes. Our prices here are the same as on Booking.com, and you pay us directly, with no middleman.
In full when you book, by card. You receive a confirmation and an invoice by email.
[Free cancellation up to 14 days before arrival, or a non-refundable rate 10% cheaper. Terms to confirm.]
Greece charges a climate resilience fee per room and night. It is paid at the hotel: [€… a night for a room, €… for the villa, April to October].

questions.q: What time is check-in and check-out?
questions.a: Check-in from 14:00, check-out by 11:00. [Ask us about an early arrival or a late departure; we will help if the room is free.]
We do not serve breakfast: every room has its own kitchen. A breakfast basket from our partner bakery costs €15 for two; order it the day before.
We welcome all guests. Our rooms are best suited to guests aged 12 and over; for families with younger children, Villa Eudora has room for everyone.
Yes, pets are welcome. [Size, number of pets and the fee to confirm.]
Yes, for all guests of the hotel and the villa. Rackets and balls are there to borrow, and the court is lit in the evening.

questions.q: Can we hold a wedding or a party at the villa?
questions.a: Yes, weddings and celebrations are welcome. Send us the date and the number of guests from the villa page.

questions.q: What is the shortest stay at the villa?
questions.a: [7 nights in July and August with Saturday arrivals, 5 nights in the rest of the season.]

about.title: About Amour
about.text: A small hotel on stone terraces above Almyrida bay, and a villa four minutes away. Built around one idea: stay like you live here.
about.label: Our philosophy
about.phrase: We believe a place to stay should feel like a home, not a hotel corridor. Your own kitchen, your own terrace, stone and olive trees around you, nothing that shouts. A quiet base to live by your own rhythm and to set out to see Crete.
